about.title: Beverly Hills Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Beverly Hills draws heavy foot traffic to its shopping districts, restaurants, hotels, and office buildings, and that traffic means more opportunities for hazards to go unaddressed — a cracked sidewalk near Wilshire Boulevard, a spill left unmarked in a boutique, a dim parking structure stairwell. Under California law, a property owner or business generally must have known, or should have known, about a dangerous condition and failed to fix or warn about it before liability attaches. That's why documenting the hazard immediately, photographing the scene, and requesting that surveillance footage be preserved can matter as much as the medical treatment you receive afterward. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly — we connect injured people in Beverly Hills with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the notice issue, gather evidence before it disappears, and explain your options under a contingency arrangement, so there's no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Notice and Evidence

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises claims turn on whether the property owner had notice of the hazard and failed to act. An attorney can help identify maintenance logs, complaint records, or inspection schedules that speak to that notice.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Footage Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many Beverly Hills stores, hotels, and office buildings overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can be the difference between having evidence and losing it.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: California applies pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery can be reduced by your share of responsibility but isn't automatically barred. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that fairly reflects what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Beverly Hills?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the fall happened on public property, such as a city sidewalk or municipal building, the deadline to file a claim is much shorter, so it's worth having an attorney review the details early.

items.question: What if the fall happened inside a hotel or retail store on Rodeo Drive or Wilshire Boulevard?
items.answer: Commercial property owners in busy Beverly Hills shopping and hotel districts are held to the same notice standard as any other property owner — they must have known or reasonably should have known about the hazard. High foot traffic can actually work in your favor, since it may show the condition existed long enough that staff should have noticed it.

items.question: Do I need to prove the store or property owner was careless?
items.answer: You generally need to show the property owner had notice of the dangerous condition and failed to address it within a reasonable time. This can include evidence like prior complaints, inspection records, or how long the hazard was visible before your fall. An independent attorney can help identify what evidence applies to your situation.
